sections.skill: Use AI translation for understanding and know its limits

questions.prompt: Which use of AI translation is generally reasonable?

choices.text: Translating an immigration form unchecked
Translating medicine instructions with no check
Translating a legal contract you will sign without any check by a fluent person
Getting the gist of a menu while traveling

questions.correct_answer: Getting the gist of a menu while traveling
questions.intro: AI translation is useful for UNDERSTANDING: reading a menu, getting the gist of an email, or having a basic conversation. It can be wrong in ways that matter: idioms translated word for word, the wrong level of politeness, names or numbers changed, or a word with two meanings translated the wrong way. For anything important, such as legal documents, medical instructions, immigration forms or contracts, use a qualified human translator or have a fluent speaker check, because errors there can cause real harm. A quick check: translate the result back into the original language and see whether the meaning survived.
questions.feedback: Understanding everyday text is a good use.

sections.skill: Compare translation with a phrase book abroad

questions.prompt: What is a phrase book good for?

choices.text: Ordering food and asking directions
Signing a contract
Explaining surgery history
Arguing a court case in another country without any other help

questions.correct_answer: Ordering food and asking directions
questions.intro: A traveler with a pocket PHRASE BOOK can order food and ask for directions: good enough to get by. But no one would use a phrase book to argue a court case or explain a medical history to a surgeon. For those, you need an interpreter who truly knows both languages. AI translation is like a very large, fast phrase book: great for getting the gist and everyday needs, risky when exact meaning matters a lot.

sections.title: Apply it

sections.skill: Account for limits of back-translation and context

questions.prompt: A back-translation matches the original perfectly. Does this prove the translation is correct?

choices.text: No; errors can cancel out or be hidden
Yes; a perfect back-translation always proves the forward translation is flawless
No; back-translation is never useful
Yes; but only for short sentences

questions.correct_answer: No; errors can cancel out or be hidden
questions.intro: Back-translation helps but is not proof: two errors can cancel out, or the back-translation can repair a mistake the reader would still see. Translation quality also varies by language pair and topic; common languages and everyday topics usually go better than rare languages or technical fields. Cultural meaning matters too: a direct translation of a joke or a polite phrase may be accurate word for word yet rude or confusing in context. When the audience matters, ask a fluent speaker who knows the context.
